info.title: Axionomy Service API
info.description: Interface-neutral problem commands, replay artifacts, lifecycle control, and Studio data.

get.summary: Check whether the native Studio engine is reachable

200.description:
A deliberately small liveness contract. A successful response proves that
the native engine adapter is reachable now; loading a cached catalog does
not.

AlgorithmPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ArtifactKey.description:
What an artifact was computed from: a request with its instance and
strategy decided. The same key always gives the same artifact.

AssessmentIssueView.description:
One structured reason why a proposal is invalid.

Subjects retain the browser-facing identities of the roles, accounts,
rates, and assets involved instead of flattening distinct failures into the
same generic error string.

ClassPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ConditionPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

DocumentPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ExactQuantity.description: An exact, non-negative quantity encoded as text for JavaScript safety.

FrameCueView.description:
A readable explanation derived from the applied exchange and its receipt.
Cues make economically meaningful transitions visible even when a domain
projection chooses identical geometry before and after the exchange.

account.description:
Optional authoritative account represented by this cell. This makes
receipt-derived cell emphasis and account inspection portable without
turning the grid projection into state of its own.

label.description:
Human-readable terrain or cell state. Renderers may keep repetitive
labels (for example, `Floor`) accessible without drawing them in every
cell.

HealthResponse.description:
A deliberately small liveness contract. A successful response proves that
the native engine adapter is reachable now; loading a cached catalog does
not.

InstanceProfile.description:
How large an instance of a problem is. Every problem has one instance of
each size.

InvariantPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ItemPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

rank.description:
Eligible entries use one-based competition ranking. Ineligible entries
remain visible but deliberately have no rank.

value.description:
Exact display text. Ratios should be reduced before projection rather
than rounded into semantic state.

MarketActorView.description:
One participant positioned around a market pool. Balances and status are
replay-derived presentation data linked back to the represented account.

MarketPoolView.description:
One constant-product pool projected from an authoritative replay snapshot.
Values remain exact text so renderers cannot silently round economic state.

MeasurePath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ModelView.description: Read-only explanation of the authoritative economy definition.

ObservationView.description:
An actor-relative observation. Omitted accounts and assets are intentionally
not visible to that actor; this is not a filtered copy of authoritative
state pretending to be complete.

ParameterPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

values.description: Ordered exactly like `ParetoFrontView.axes`; values remain exact text.

PhasePath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ProblemPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ProposalPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

ProposalView.description: A proposal assessed against an exact snapshot, including rejected actions.

RateRoleView.description: A rate role's complete consume/produce/preserve contract.

RateView.description: One immutable transition rule in the closed model.

selected_document.description: The document of the requested strategy.

RunRequest.description:
A request to run a problem. The instance and strategy default to the
problem's own.

key.description: What the run's artifact was computed from, once it is published.

Scene.description:
Optional problem picture derived from the economic state.
Pictures explain and animate; they never decide whether an exchange applies.

oneOf.description:
Attach presentation state to another stable scene entity. This is used
for inventory, cargo, equipment, and similar ownership relationships
that would be misleading if attached only to a shared location.

SceneEntityRoleView.description:
How a semantic entity relates to the geometric surface it is anchored to.

This is presentation metadata only. It lets generic viewers distinguish a
place from something occupying it, a task attached to it, state describing
it, or scenario context that should remain outside the topology.

status.description: A short status line for people, such as `2 crates aboard`.

SceneEvidenceRefView.description:
Exact economic evidence illustrated by a disposable scene entity.

These references never create state or authorize a transition. They let a
renderer connect replay-derived motion and emphasis back to the accounts
and balances that prove why the picture changed.

SceneGlyphView.description:
A semantic icon key owned by the portable Rust contract. The browser maps
these keys to its chosen icon implementation; documents never contain SVG,
CSS class names masquerading as meaning, or React component names.

value.description: Exact text preserves arbitrarily large quantities and caller units.

SceneSurfaceView.description:
The geometric substrate for a derived scene. Surface geometry and semantic
entities are deliberately separate so one vehicle can move through a graph,
grid, matrix, or timeline without inventing four domain models.

SearchObservationView.description:
A bounded, transport-neutral view of solver work. Search crates expose
typed session state; the service maps it into this presentation contract so
HTTP, WASM, saved artifacts, and Studio use identical evidence.

subjects.description:
Stable Rust-owned scene subjects affected by this observation. Generic
viewers may emphasize matching nodes or entities without understanding
the problem's domain model.

algorithm.description: The algorithm in words, such as `breadth-first search`.

StrategyPath.description: Lowercase segments of a–z, 0–9 and `-`, separated by `/`, such as `loans/42`; each segment starts and ends with a letter or digit.

StudioEvent.description:
Lifecycle events emitted by a Studio run. `sequence` orders transport
events; it is not economic time and has no effect on replay.

oneOf.description: The run's artifact can be fetched.

StudioRunId.description: A Studio run: `run-` and a number, such as `run-7`.

TelemetryPointView.description:
A transport-neutral progress observation. Counters are exact text so the
same contract remains safe in native and JavaScript consumers.

solve_observations.description:
Bounded solver history retained so a fast native run or a static Pages
artifact is as inspectable as a live stream.

ViewId.description:
A browser-safe identity for an arbitrary user-defined ontology value.

`key` is used for joins, `label` is for people, and `value` is optional
diagnostic context. None of these fields replaces the underlying Rust value
as semantic authority.

leaderboards.description:
Disposable rankings derived from this exact replay-verified state.
They explain comparative outcomes; they never authorize an exchange.
